answer: The strongest lever is simple: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because ivory only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. In practice pearl is enforced by the ledger itself: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any karst approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
